common_name: Pink Charm Redbud (Withers Pink Charm Clear-Pink Selection)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in late winter, spring, or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Pink Charm is an older named selection grown from grafted or cutting-propagated stock to preserve its distinct clear-pink flower color.

directions: Pink Charm is a long-grown named selection of eastern redbud chosen for flowers of a clean, unambiguous pink rather than the purplish-pink buds and blooms typical of wild seedling trees. It flowers heavily on bare branches in early spring, forming a dense pastel haze before the heart-shaped leaves unfold, then carries clean green summer foliage typical of the species. As an understory tree it tolerates a half-day of shade without losing vigor, though flowering is fullest with at least a half day of direct sun. Site it where its distinctive flower color can be compared directly with a standard seedling redbud for the contrast.

planting.note: Plant grafted or rooted-cutting container stock in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Burgundy Hearts was selected by Greenleaf Nurseries from a large block of seedlings for improved foliage color retention compared to older purple-leaf redbuds.

directions: Burgundy Hearts opens with pinkish-lavender pea-shaped flowers along bare branches in early spring, then unfurls heart-shaped leaves in a lustrous reddish-purple that holds its depth through summer heat noticeably longer than older dark-leaf redbud selections before shifting toward wine-red tones in fall. It tolerates more direct sun than many purple-leaf redbuds without the foliage scorching or fading to green, making it a reliable specimen or accent tree for sunnier sites. Give it well-drained soil, since redbuds as a group resent waterlogging at the root zone. Prune only to shape or remove damaged wood right after the spring flowers fade.

common_name: Pauline Lily Redbud (Pale Pink-to-White Flowered Selection)

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Pauline Lily tolerates clay soil and sites near black walnut better than many ornamental trees, making it a useful option where soil chemistry limits other choices.

directions: Pauline Lily is a named redbud selection grown for its pale, soft pink buds that open to a light pinkish-white flower, a subtler color break from the species' typical rosy-purple blooms rather than a bold departure like the pure white forms. It flowers on bare wood in April ahead of the leaves, then settles into typical rounded, heart-shaped green summer foliage. It is notably tolerant of clay soil and of growing near black walnut trees, a juglone sensitivity that limits many other ornamentals, making it a practical choice for difficult sites. Grow it in full sun to partial shade with average garden water and minimal pruning beyond removing damaged wood.
sources: North Shore Plant Club plant database

common_name: Vanilla Twist Weeping Redbud (Dwarf White-Flowered Weeping Selection)

planting.note: Plant grafted, top-worked nursery stock in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Vanilla Twist is a dwarf weeping form, a cross of 'Royal White' and 'Covey', typically trained on a staked standard trunk to show off its cascading habit.

directions: Vanilla Twist is a dwarf weeping redbud bred from a cross of white-flowered 'Royal White' and the pink weeping 'Covey', producing creamy white, sweetpea-shaped flowers along pendulous, umbrella-like branches in early spring. Broad heart-shaped leaves follow in a soft copper-green that matures to blue-green, giving the cascading canopy interest beyond the bloom period. Because the habit mounds and weeps rather than growing upright, nursery stock is almost always top-grafted onto a standard trunk, so the leader should be staked while young until the desired head height is reached. It needs little pruning beyond removing any upright reversion shoots from below the graft.
sources: Utah State University Extension Botanical Center

planting.note: Plant grafted or rooted-cutting container stock in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; Midnight Express was introduced through the Proven Winners ColorChoice program as a darker-leaved, more heat-tolerant alternative to older purple-leaf redbud selections.

directions: Midnight Express carries lavender-pink pea-shaped flowers along bare branches in early spring before unfurling heart-shaped leaves in an unusually deep, near-black purple that resists the summer green-out common in older dark-foliage redbud cultivars. The intensified, long-lasting foliage color is its main selling point over earlier selections such as Forest Pansy, holding its depth well into late summer even in hot, humid regions. Give it a full-sun to lightly shaded site with well-drained soil, since deeper shade tends to mute the dark coloration. Prune lightly right after flowering to remove crossing or damaged branches.

common_name: Royal White Redbud (Vigorous Large-Flowered White Selection)

planting.note: Plant container or balled-and-burlapped trees in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Royal White is an older, vigorous white-flowered selection used as a parent of several newer weeping white redbud cultivars.

directions: Royal White is an established pure-white-flowered redbud selection valued for heavier, larger-flowered bloom than the typical white seedling form, opening on bare branches ahead of the foliage in early spring. Growth is vigorous and the overall habit matches the species: a rounded, multi-branched small tree with clean green, heart-shaped summer leaves. Its reliable white flower color and good vigor have made it a parent in breeding newer cultivars, including weeping white-flowered selections. Grow it in full sun to partial shade in well-drained soil, pruning only to remove damaged or crossing wood after bloom.
sources: Utah State University Extension Botanical Center
